title: I Used the Conference Badge-Reprint Math Through Three Days

parts.text: Day one billed reprint fees on badges the house had misprinted. The exhibitor contract I signed said: REPRINTS ON ATTENDEE ERRORS ONLY. I was forty-nine, nonprofit treasurer, holding an invoice with a $420 line. I queried it. They said "house is an attendee of the hall." I paid under protest and waited for day two.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Day two is tomorrow and the protest letter is already in the file.

social.video_title: They billed reprints on the house misprint — Part 1/3
social.description: 420 dollars, a contract line, house as attendee. Protest is filed. Would you have paid quietly?

parts.text: Day two they billed reprints on lanyards they had snapped at a toast I did not authorize. I was still forty-nine, still the file. I added the lanyard invoice to the protest and asked for the print count from their own POS. POS showed 18 reprints. They had billed 40. I forwarded the POS to the convention controller and put a hold on day three's deposit.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The deposit is on hold and day three's rider is already at legal.

social.video_title: They billed 40 reprints when POS showed 18 — Part 2/3
social.description: Unauthorized toast, POS math, a held deposit. Legal has the rider. Does the house still feel like an attendee?

parts.text: Day three ran on a rider: REPRINTS = ATTENDEE ERRORS SCANNED IN. House misprints came off the invoice entirely. They credited $420 and the ghost 22 badges. I wore a badge we printed, scanned. Optics is a word halls use when POS exists. The math survived three mornings. The week finally cost what the contract said, which is a kind of lanyard.

social.video_title: Reprints became a scan, not a vibe — Part 3/3
social.description: Credits posted, a rider, attendee errors scanned. Was the house ever an attendee?
